why: We want AI to save time on activity plans and paperwork. We must keep children's information safe and follow our district agreement.
who_it_covers: Staff, group leaders, volunteers, contractors and board members at all four sites.
new_tools: Renee approves any new tool, plugin, agent or AI feature in software we already use. Joy checks settings first. The district must also agree if student data is involved.
accounts: Use a work account where you have one, and turn off any setting that lets the vendor train on what you type.
everyone_now: Use any AI tool, signed in with a work email, for work with no information about a real child, family, donor or staff member.
allowed_uses: Group leaders: activity plans and activity ideas.
Group leaders: STEM projects and games.
Site directors: drafting schedules and the weekly parent newsletter.

needs_approval.use: Grant reports and outcomes data for the state or funders
Student information, only inside the district platform's own tools

protected_information: These stay out of AI tools unless a tool is approved for them above: student names, photos, video, grades, test scores, attendance, IEP and 504 details, allergies, medications, custody and pickup information, incident reports, donor names and spreadsheet, staff and volunteer details, passwords and login details. Our district data-sharing agreement covers student records.
off_limits: Mandated reporting. If you suspect abuse, you call it in. AI never touches it.
Never paste incident reports or notes about a child's behavior into AI.
No AI-generated images of our kids.
No AI-edited photos of real kids.
check_before_it_goes_out: You are responsible for anything you send, even if AI wrote it.
Check facts, names, times, dates and numbers. A wrong pickup time can leave a child waiting.
A person checks grant report numbers against our records before anything goes to the state.
decisions_about_people: AI never decides who gets services, a place in our program, or a consequence for a child.
Staff write incident reports and notes about a child's behavior themselves.
being_open: Translated newsletters say they were machine-translated, so parents know to ask if something looks wrong.
We tell parents about any AI use with their kids.
if_something_goes_wrong: Tell your site director the same day. Site directors tell Renee the same day.
Reporting a mistake is expected. Nobody is punished for it.
who_owns_this: The owner makes sure staff and volunteers see this policy.
open_questions: Can kids use AI during homework hour, and do we follow each school's rule or make our own?
Which AI tools, if any, will we approve or pay for, such as Gemini or ChatGPT, and do group leaders have work emails?
May we use AI to translate the newsletter, and who checks the Vietnamese version before it goes out?
Should the board approve this policy and later changes?
